title: 3rd Party � Claims Company � Claim NOT Opened � Non-EU Country � User Disputes � Manual Handoff
goal: Validates that when a claims company is rejected on the "no claim opened" + non-EU path but disputes, the system escalates to manual handoff.

checkpoints.step: Validates that when a claims company is rejected on the "no claim opened" + non-EU path but disputes, the system escalates to manual handoff.
Third-party caller type: Claims Company
Passenger has NOT opened a claim
checkpoints.expected: Passenger has NOT opened a claim

checkpoints.step: Country of origin: US
User disputes rejection
Given the user opens the agentic chatbot
Then the chatbot displays greeting (GLOB-01)
Then user selects English
Then chatbot asks "How can I help you today?"
checkpoints.expected: How can I help you today?

checkpoints.step: And the user says "Claims company here, I need to file a disruption claim for a passenger"
checkpoints.expected: Claims company here, I need to file a disruption claim for a passenger

checkpoints.step: When the chatbot identifies flight disruption intent
Then the chatbot checks: Is this a third-party submission? ? YES
Then the chatbot identifies third-party type ? Claims Company
Then the chatbot asks: "Has a claim been opened by the passenger?"
checkpoints.expected: Has a claim been opened by the passenger?

checkpoints.step: And the user responds: "No"
Then the chatbot asks: "From which country did the person you are claiming for originate?"
checkpoints.expected: From which country did the person you are claiming for originate?

checkpoints.step: And the user provides: "United States"

Then the chatbot responds: "Claims for flight disruption which occurred in United States must be submitted by the passenger who experienced the disruption. Third parties cannot submit claims for disruption that occur in United States. Please advise the passenger to open a claim themselves."
checkpoints.expected: Claims for flight disruption which occurred in United States must be submitted by the passenger who experienced the disruption. Third parties cannot submit claims for disruption that occur in United States. Please advise the passenger to open a claim themselves.

checkpoints.step: And the user responds: "We have legal authorization and insist on proceeding"

Then the chatbot responds: "Thanks, a few questions for me to forward your claim: Please provide the name of claims company, ticket number, booking reference, contact information for the passenger, full passenger names for your claim. You'll also need to upload the power of attorney or notice of authorization to have your claim actioned."
checkpoints.expected: Thanks, a few questions for me to forward your claim: Please provide the name of claims company, ticket number, booking reference, contact information for the passenger, full passenger names for your claim. You'll also need to upload the power of attorney or notice of authorization to have your claim actioned.

checkpoints.step: And the user provides all required information
Then the system creates a case and routes it for manual handling
Then the chatbot offers: "Is there anything I can help you with?"
checkpoints.expected: Is there anything I can help you with?

checkpoints.step: And the user selects "No"
Then the chatbot responds "Thank you for choosing Air Canada."
checkpoints.expected: Thank you for choosing Air Canada.

checkpoints.step: Given the system rejects for non-EU country
And the user disputes the rejection
Then the system should override and proceed to manual handoff with full info collection
And a case should be created for manual handling
And the Claims Dashboard should show the case with dispute override noted
And this mirrors TC187 but on the "no claim opened" branch
Given the third-party submission with no claim opened was accepted via dispute override
Then no automated payment flow should be triggered
And the case should be in manual review status
